parsed.explanation: Documented national regime criminalises same-sex conduct but is operative against gender presentation: trans/gender-nonconforming visitors may be arrested, detained, beaten, prosecuted and sentenced up to five years, with prison described as hell. Appeals sometimes release or acquit, but protections are thin, an LGBTQ organisation was shut, few lawyers act, and police/gendarmes continue arbitrary detention. Border screening, marker protection and care access are unresolved, not safe. Missing resident-only machinery is not counted against the traveller. Discovery therefore carries severe non-lethal but imprisonable exposure. Minor/guardian-specific rules are undocumented, while adult travellers with minors likely enter the same regime. Execution is not documented, but imprisonment, abuse and weak remedy keep the score near severe-risk ceiling.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented for ports of entry. A failed-identification charge accompanied a trans-related prosecution, suggesting document mismatch can aggravate once inside.
entry_documents.protection: Not documented. No recognition, marker protection, or traveler-facing entry rule is evidenced; absence of evidence is not safety.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry screening unresolved, but domestic identity checks can arise after arrival.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Arrests for gender presentation, detention for months, beatings in custody, prison called hell, few willing lawyers, LGBTQ organisation shut after raid.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Appeals can order release pending hearing; one dress-based conviction was acquitted on appeal, showing limited judicial relief.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Investigation for presentation can feed prosecution and harsh custody; relief is case-by-case and slow.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No formal bathroom or service ban documented, but detention facilities, public restaurant arrests and prison conditions are hostile.
federal_state_facilities.protection: None documented. Subnational record is incident-level; no protective facility rule shown.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: National criminalisation applied in commercial city and nationally in 2022 arrests; local facilities lack documented mitigation.

care_services.exposure: Not documented. Coercive medical-exam threat is recorded, but hormone therapy, emergency care or medication access rules are not.
care_services.protection: Not documented. No care access or confidentiality protection shown.
care_services.interaction: A health incident could expose a trans traveller to coercive or absent care, but the operative care regime is unresolved.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Penal and cybercrime provisions criminalise presentation-linked conduct; police/gendarmes arbitrarily detain and beat people; press outings occurred.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: A state council criticised a privacy breach, but prosecutions continued; no anti-discrimination machinery documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Law frames trans/gender-nonconforming appearance as criminal, enabling both civilian abuse and official misconduct.

minors_guardians.exposure: No minor-specific rule documented; the same presentation-based criminalisation could apply to a trans minor or nonconforming child.
minors_guardians.protection: Not documented. No guardian immunity, child protection, or family-friendly care is shown.
minors_guardians.interaction: Guardians could face document checks or service refusals alongside minors; effects unresolved.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Beatings of gay and trans people described as common; group attacks and arbitrary security-force arrests documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Occasional appellate release/acquittal; no effective police accountability or trans-specific protection shown.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Public violence and police abuse reinforce each other; reporting risks extortion or false allegations.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Thin remedies: few lawyers, NGO closed, prison abuse, cyber/offline enforcement, appeal outcomes incomplete.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Appeals sometimes succeeded, and one trans woman was released pending appeal before fleeing.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies depend on slow courts and political context; unresolved border and care gaps mean unknowns remain risk.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar to 0.15-A in appearance-based criminalisation, detention, beatings and weak effective remedies. Slightly safer because no capital provision or routine border/transport checks are documented, but five-year maximum sentences and harsh prison keep it severe.

Below 0.25-A. That anchor includes detention, fines, raids and rare imprisonment; this dossier documents actual sentences up to the maximum statutory term, beatings and prison abuse, indicating higher severity.

Materially worse than 0.55-A. That anchor has registration/checkpoint friction and possible holding without credible severe punishment; here gender presentation itself feeds multi-year prosecutions and abusive custody.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime combines a broadly criminalising law with enforcement against gender presentation. Visitors are not documented to face entry screening, but if presentation is read as trans or nonconforming they may be arrested, beaten, prosecuted and imprisoned up to five years, including failed-ID charges. Institutions are hostile: police/gendarmes abuse with impunity, an LGBTQ organisation was shut, few lawyers defend cases, and prison conditions are severe. Appeals occasionally provide relief, and no execution is documented, which prevents a catastrophic endpoint score, but these are partial and not traveller-facing protections. Missing border and care rules remain uncertain, not safe. Adult-alone and adult-with-minor travellers likely enter the same severe exposure regime.
